info.bio:
Exodus es un grupo de thrash metal formado en 1979 en San Francisco, California, por Tom Hunting, Paul Baloff y Gary Holt. En 1983 Kirk Hammett fue a formar parte de Metallica y fue reemplazado por Rick Hunolt. Rob McKillop fue reclutado como bajista. Poco antes del lanzamiento de Pleasures Of The Flesh en 1987, Paul Baloff se fue de la banda y fue reemplazado por Steve "Zetro" Souza.

En los inicios del movimiento del thrash metal Exodus era la agrupación más extrema.

scenes.name: Speed/thrash metal
scenes.book: Heavy Metal: The Music and Its Culture
scenes.author: Deena Weinstein
scenes.desc: Si el lite metal es la corriente latitudinaria, el speed/thrash es la fundamentalista: un retorno a los principios de la subcultura heavy que, como todo fundamentalismo, es tanto un comienzo nuevo como una continuación. Nace en California en 1981-83 con Metallica en Los Ángeles y Exodus en San Francisco; hacia 1982 hay una escena de fans que intercambian maquetas y grabaciones piratas, y durante años solo graba en sellos independientes y suena en programas de radio universitaria: «underground» también en lo comercial. Bebe de la NWOBHM (Venom, Diamond Head, Iron Maiden) y del punk y el hardcore. Weinstein lo compara con la Reforma protestante: fuera la ropa de escena, el atrezo y la distancia; los músicos visten vaqueros y camiseta, se mezclan con el público y se tiran a él desde el escenario. Acelera el tempo, renuncia a lo dionisíaco (el alcohol y las drogas son malos, no hay sexo) y se especializa en un caos concreto: alienación, corrupción política, destrucción ambiental, una retórica de canción protesta.

scenes.name: La bestia ha vuelto: OzzFest y las reuniones
scenes.book: Heavy Metal: The Music and Its Culture
scenes.author: Deena Weinstein
scenes.desc: A finales de siglo el metal vuelve a la corriente principal. Con el alternativo moribundo y la electrónica sin despegar, el público fiel sigue ahí: tres mil personas esperan cinco horas en un centro comercial de Chicago en 1998 a que Black Sabbath les firme discos. El detonante es el OzzFest de 1997, organizado por la mánager de Ozzy, que vende más que Lollapalooza con Pantera, Machine Head, Fear Factory, Type O Negative, Neurosis, tres cuartas partes de Black Sabbath y Marilyn Manson, cuyas provocaciones atraen protestas cristianas y titulares. Metallica vuelve a tocar su thrash en directo y en Garage Inc.; Judas Priest ficha a Tim «Ripper» Owens, cantante de una banda tributo llamada British Steel; Mötley Crüe recupera a Vince Neil, Kiss se reúne en 1998, Dickinson regresa a Iron Maiden y Black Sabbath hace en 1999 una gira de reunión con disco de oro. Weinstein ve en ese regreso el gusto «prole» de la cultura de fin de siglo, un contrapeso a la feminización del pop y la ansiedad milenarista: la bestia se niega a morir.

scenes.name: Speed y thrash metal
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: La escena «street» de Los Ángeles cruza el hardcore (Bad Brains, Black Flag) con el glam-metal. A partir de una intuición de D.R.I., Metallica inventan el speed-metal: del thrash de Kill 'Em All a la elegancia casi clásica de Master Of Puppets. Megadeth, Slayer (puente entre el black metal de Venom y el death metal), Exciter, la escena de San Francisco (Death Angel, Exodus, Testament), Anthrax y White Zombie en Nueva York, y Sepultura, que lo convierten en lenguaje universal (Roots).

xref.title: Pre-1970 Exodus to US
xref.body: Before 1970, with Canada lacking a developed music industry, Neil Young was among the "biggest and most promising artists" who felt compelled to move to the United States to "actually make a living." "Neil Young, Jody Mitchell, Paul Anke, Leonard Cohen, all of our biggest and most promising artists beat a path for the United States."

xref.title: Anthony Kiedis's Rehab and Relapses (1994-1997)
xref.body: Kiedis's first serious rehab stint led to five years of sobriety, but he relapsed in January 1994 after a wisdom tooth extraction led to prescription narcotics (Vicodin and Percodan) and a return to cocaine and heroin. This cycle of getting straight and relapsing continued until 1997, including a stay at Exodus Recovery Center in Marina Del Rey, California. "His first serious trip to rehab left him sober for five years, but then there was a relapse in January 1994 when he had a wisdom tooth removed and the dentist put him on narcotics for the pain, which was a really bad idea."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Death and Rehab Attempt (1994)
xref.body: Kurt Cobain's death was reported on April 8, 1994, affecting Dave Gahan during Depeche Mode's tour in Buenos Aires. Cobain had also attempted to get clean at the Exodus Recovery Center in Marino Del Rey, California, a week before his death. "De Peshmoan was in Buenos Aires on April 8, 1994 when they heard about the death of Kurt Cobain."

xref.title: Death by Suicide (April 5, 1994)
xref.body: Kurt Cobain died in the early morning of Tuesday, April 5, 1994, by suicide via shotgun, preceded by a massive heroin overdose. His body was found approximately two weeks later, on April 8. His family and friends were aware he was in trouble, especially after a previous suicide attempt at a hotel in Rome. On March 25, 1994, an intervention was held at his Seattle home with his wife Courtney Love, bandmates Chris Novoselic and Dave Grohl, touring guitarist Pat Smear, and members of Nirvana's management and legal team, lasting five hours. He seemed convinced to seek help and flew to LA on March 30 to check into the Exodus Recovery Center. However, he left on April 1 (Good Friday) by scaling a six-foot wall, flew back to Seattle, and disappeared. His final note, addressed to his imaginary friend "Boddah," was found in his pocket after he injected a large amount of Mexican black tar heroin and then used a Remington shotgun to kill himself in the greenhouse at his home. "He had injected so much heroin that he probably never even heard the gun go off."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Disappearance from Rehab (1994)
xref.body: On April 1, 1994, Kurt Cobain disappeared from the Exodus Recovery Center in Los Angeles after spending two nights in the facility. He subsequently flew back to Seattle the following morning. "On April 1, 1994, Kurt disappeared from the Exodus Recovery Center in Los Angeles."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Escape from Rehab (April 1994)
xref.body: While at the Exodus Recovery Center, Kurt Cobain befriended fellow patient Gibby Haynes of the Butthole Surfers. On the evening of Good Friday, April 1st, 1994, at 7:25 PM, Cobain told an attendant he was going for a smoke, then scaled a six-foot fence to escape, despite being able to simply walk out under Exodus policy. "Instead, he scaled the six-foot fence and made a break for it, which was unnecessarily dramatic, since under Exodus policy, he could have just walked out the front door."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Exodus Recovery Center Escape (April 1, 1994)
xref.body: Kurt checked into the Exodus Recovery Center in Los Angeles on March 30, but after two nights, on the evening of Good Friday, April 1st, he scaled a garden wall, took a cab to the airport, and caught Delta flight 788 back to Seattle. "But on the evening of Good Friday, April 1st, he scaled the wall in the garden, took a cab to the airport where he caught Delta flight 788 to Seattle."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Exodus Recovery Center Stay (Spring 1994)
xref.body: Gibby Haynes was present at the Exodus Recovery Center in Marina del Rey during spring 1994, at the same time Scott Wyland was considering checking into the facility for detox, leading to Wyland's decision not to check in. "There are two major junkies already on the premises and that will not help you kick your habit."

xref.body: Kurt Cobain was a 27-year-old from Seattle who was at the Exodus Recovery Center in Marina del Rey during spring 1994, at the same time Scott Wyland was considering checking into the facility for detox. "The second was a 27 year old guy from Seattle named Kurt Cobain."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: First Detox Attempt (Spring 1994) – Exodus Recovery Center
xref.body: In spring 1994, Wyland intended to check into the Exodus Recovery Center in Marina del Rey for detox. He was advised against it because two other "major junkies," Gibby Haynes of the Butthole Surfers (who allegedly introduced Wyland to heroin) and Kurt Cobain, were already present. "There are two major junkies already on the premises and that will not help you kick your habit."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Intervention and Brief Rehab Stay (March 25-April 1, 1994)
xref.body: On March 25, 1994, an intervention was held for Kurt Cobain, involving Nirvana members Krist Novoselic and Dave Grohl, guitarist Pat Smear, management and legal team members, doctors, and drug counselor James Burr. The five-hour meeting persuaded Kurt to enter rehab, and he communicated his intention to rest and recover via his AOL account. On March 30, he checked into the Exodus Recovery Center in Los Angeles but departed just two days later on April 1, scaling a guard wall despite having checked in voluntarily. "That meeting lasted five hours. Kurt was convinced to try rehab and arrangements were made."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Intervention and Second Rehab Stint (1994)
xref.body: On March 25th, 1994, an intervention by friends, family, and business associates convinced Kurt Cobain to address his self-destructive behavior and heroin addiction. He reluctantly agreed to try rehab again, checking into the Exodus Recovery Center in Los Angeles on Thursday, March 30th. "On March 25th, 1994, an intervention of friends, family, and business associates convinced Kurt that his self-destructive tendencies brought on by his heroin issues had to stop, so he reluctantly and angrily agreed to try rehab again."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Rehab Check-in and Escape (1994)
xref.body: Following the intervention, Kurt Cobain appeared convinced to seek help and flew to Los Angeles on March 30th to check into the Exodus Recovery Center, a rehab facility known for treating struggling celebrities. However, after spending only two nights there, he scaled a six-foot garden wall on the evening of Good Friday, April 1st, to escape, despite the terms of his stay allowing him to simply walk out the front door. "Kurt went to LA and checked into the Exodus recovery center that night. He spent two nights. But on the evening of Good Friday, able the first, he scaled the six-foot wall on the garden, which was kind of weird since the terms of his stay would have allowed him to just walk out the front door and check himself out."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Rehab Companion to Kurt Cobain (1994)
xref.body: While at the Exodus Recovery Center in Los Angeles in 1994, Gibby Haynes of the Butthole Surfers was a fellow patient and friend to Kurt Cobain. They "hung out and commiserated about their respective situations." "One of the other patients was Gibby Haines of the Butthole Surfers."

xref.title: Rehab and Escape (March 30 - April 1, 1994)
xref.body: On March 30, 1994, Kurt Cobain flew to Los Angeles to check into the Exodus Recovery Center, a rehab unit known for helping celebrities. He spent two nights there. However, on the evening of Good Friday, April 1, he scaled a six-foot garden wall to escape, despite the terms of his stay allowing him to simply walk out the front door. He then took a taxi to LAX and flew back to Seattle on Delta Flight 788. "He spent two nights, but on the evening of Good Friday able the first, he scaled the six-foot wall on the garden, which was kind of weird since the terms of his stay would have allowed him to just walk out the front door and check himself out."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Clinical Death and Court-Ordered Rehab (1996)
xref.body: On May 27th, 1996, after working on new material in New York, Gahan returned to Los Angeles, checked into the Sunset Marquis, and injected a potent mix of heroin and cocaine. He suffered a massive overdose, was found clinically dead for two minutes by paramedics at 1:15 AM on May 28th. After being released from the hospital, he immediately used drugs again but experienced no high. A court-ordered stay at the Exodus Recovery Center in Los Angeles appeared to finally establish his sobriety, which has reportedly continued ever since. "When paramedics arrived, Dave had been clinically dead for two minutes."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Post-Clinical Death Relapse and Recovery (1996)
xref.body: Despite being released from the hospital and jail on $10,000 bail for drug charges after his near-fatal overdose, Dave Gahan immediately returned to using heroin, though it no longer provided any buzz. This realization prompted him to check into the Exodus Recovery Center in Marino Del Rey, California, a facility where Kurt Cobain and Shannon Hoon also sought treatment. In Dave's case, the treatment was successful, leading to his sobriety. "But in Dave's case, the treatment worked."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Introducing "Uncharted": Depeche Mode and the Debauched Devotional Tour

xref.title: Post-Overdose Recovery (1996)
xref.body: Following his release from the hospital and subsequently from jail on drug charges after his massive overdose in May 1996, Dave Gahan immediately returned to using heroin ("smack"). However, this time, he experienced no "buzz" or effect from the drug. This profound lack of sensation prompted him to voluntarily admit himself to the Exodus Recovery Center in Marina del Rey, California, a facility notably known for having treated Kurt Cobain shortly before his death. At Exodus, Gahan embraced accountability for his actions, achieved sobriety, cleaned up, and has reportedly maintained a clean and straight lifestyle since late 1998. "But this time, there was no buzz. There was nothing."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Connections to Other Metal Bands
xref.body: In addition to his work with Testament, Chuck Billy has contributed to another metal band, Exodus, and was once considered for the role of frontman for Sepultura. He is also friends with many other prominent figures in the metal scene. "In addition to working with Testament, he's also contributed to Exodus, another metal band. And once had a shot at being the frontman for Sepulchura. He's also friends with a ton of other big name metal dudes."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Rehab Attempt (1990s)
xref.body: Shannon Hoon, the singer for Blind Melon, also attempted to get clean at the Exodus Recovery Center in Marino Del Rey, California, the same facility where Dave Gahan eventually found sobriety. "It was also where Shannon Hoon of Blind Melon tried to get straight."
